text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified all of these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Food and detergent group Unilever puts its chemicals sector up for sale. (p1)
- Former Philips chairman Jan Timmer unexpectedly resigns as supervisory board member. (p1)
- Interest on ten-years bond loans drops to a historic low at 5.47 pct. (p1)
- PC maker Tulip is seeking a partnership with a producer of consumer electronics or a publisher. (p1)
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM is eyeing local Asian and South American cabin crew. (p3)
- Textile maker Textielgroep Twenthe books Dfl 0.5 million 1996 net against three million guilders losses in 1995. (p3)
- Engineering consultancy Fugro reports provisional 1996 net more than doubled to Dfl 35 million on 25 pct turnover growth. (p4)
- Machine maker Nedap raises 1996 dividend by 45 pct. (p4)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Net profit of Unilever up at Dfl 4.2 bn, mainly as a result of restructuring measures. (p2) - ABN Amro bank has given information on Indonesian union leader Pakpahan to the court.
- Dutch PTT KPN and paper and packaging group KNP BT settle conflict over their names; KPN to help pay for changing KNP BT's name. (p2)
- General director of Endemol Live Entertainment resigns after only eight months. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Fraud at ABN Amro bank, which De Telegraaf reported yesterday, amounts to only one million guilders instead of 140 million guilders. (p1)
- Soccer association KNVB gets Dfl 44 million from bankrupt sports-only TV Channel Sport 7.
- Strike actions threaten at steel maker Hoogovens. (p3)
- Automation company Getronics closes participation agreement with U.S. software giant ACI. (p21)
TROUW
- A number of Dutch economists oppose the European economic and monetary union EMU. (p1)
- Kas-Associatie bank's 1996 net rises from Dfl 14.6 million to Dfl 24.1 million. (p18)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Central planning bureau CPB forecasts continuing economic growth and strong drop in unemployment for this and next year.
